newsitem.title: UK: Metals prices in new declines.
newsitem.headline: Metals prices in new declines.

text.p: Copper prices sagged on Friday to end the week precariously hovering below $1,900 per tonne as a new wave of negative sentiment swept world metals markets.
Aluminium hit its lowest in 2-1/4 years. Gold and silver also weakened with silver at an 18-month low.

Speculative sales hit copper again crimping a rally up from $1,850 a week ago -- a level it threatened to revisit after Friday's $36 drop to the London Metal Exchange (LME) afternoon close exactly at $1,900.
Copper weakened again by some $20 in late inter-office activity. Dealers cited an emerging contango when forward values are higher than the nearby delivery price.

Copper had been in steep backwardation with spot supply commanding a premium recently when star trader Yasuo Hamanaka, sacked in June by Japan's Sumitomo Corp, was building stocks in an apparent bid to defend a high price.

Traders said the fundamental picture post-Hamanaka is now clearer. Despite falling warehouse stocks and a pick-up in physical interest in Europe, the market now believes that an oversupply in copper will be the feature in 1997. Aluminium clawed up from Friday's new 2-1/4 year low of $1,403 on end-week covering and technical support. But traders saw it below $1,400 soon.
Warehouse stocks are seen continuing to rise after a jump of 4,825 tonnes reported on Friday by the LME.
The precious metals slid after a plunge in silver below the key $5.00 level as disillusioned investors baled out.
Silver closed in London at $4.87 an ounce, a 14-cent drop from the previous finish in a sell-off that orginated in New York futures on Thursday.
Gold closed London $1.10 lower at $381.75 an ounce.
Other commodities ended the week less volatile with Chicago wheat futures just firmer, coffee extending a decline and sugar easing slightly.
Crude oil continued to shed gains recorded at the height of recent tension between the United States and Iraq. Some key commodity prices as at 1600 GMT on Friday
